input: Read /data/export.tsv which is tab-separated with columns: id, last_name, first_name, email, department. Convert it to /data/import.csv (comma-separated) with columns reordered to: email, first_name, last_name, department (dropping the id column). Include a header row. Print the result.

transcript.final_response:
Created `/data/import.csv` with the requested columns and header:

```csv
email,first_name,last_name,department
alice@co.com,Alice,Smith,Eng
bob@co.com,Bob,Jones,Sales
carol@co.com,Carol,Davis,Eng
dave@co.com,Dave,Wilson,HR
```
tool_calls:
python3 - <<'PY'
import csv
src='/data/export.tsv'
out='/data/import.csv'
with open(src, newline='', encoding='utf-8') as f_in, open(out, 'w', newline='', encoding='utf-8') as f_out:
    reader=csv.DictReader(f_in, delimiter='\t')
    fields=['email','first_name','last_name','department']
    writer=csv.DictWriter(f_out, fieldnames=fields)
    writer.writeheader()
    for row in reader:
        writer.writerow({k: row[k] for k in fields})
with open(out, encoding='utf-8', newline='') as f:
    print(f.read(), end='')
PY
